Accumulation, Antiderivatives & Differential Flows: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, the accumulation function \(A(x) = \int_a^x f(t)\,dt\) satisfies \(A'(x) = f(x)\), linking instantaneous rates of change to net signed area. In first-order differential equations \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = g(x)h(y)\), separation of variables \(\int \dfrac{1}{h(y)}\,dy = \int g(x)\,dx + C\) reconstructs the family of integral curves across the slope field.

body.en:
Why Integration by Parts & Integrating Factors Work: Differentiating a product \(u(x)v(x)\) gives \((uv)' = u'v + uv'\). Integrating both sides and rearranging yields the Integration by Parts formula:

\[ \int u\,\frac{dv}{dx}\,dx = u v - \int v\,\frac{du}{dx}\,dx \]

Similarly, for a linear first-order ODE \(y' + P(x)y = Q(x)\), multiplying by the integrating factor \(\mu(x) = e^{\int P(x)\,dx}\) (which satisfies \(\mu'(x) = P(x)\mu(x)\)) collapses the left-hand side into an exact product derivative: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\bigl[\mu(x)y\bigr] = \mu(x)Q(x)\).

label.en: ⚠️ Cambridge 9709 Traps — Parts Signs & Substitution Limits

body.en:
Signs in Integration by Parts: In \(\int u \frac{dv}{dx}dx = uv - \int v \frac{du}{dx}dx\), double negative signs are the primary source of lost marks. When \(v\) involves a negative sign (e.g. \(\int \sin x\,dx = -\cos x\)), the minus-minus becomes a plus: \(u(-\cos x) - \int(-\cos x)u'dx = -u\cos x + \int u'\cos x\,dx\).

Definite Substitution Limits: When using substitution \(u = g(x)\) on a definite integral, immediately transform both limits to \(u\)-values: \(u_1 = g(a)\) and \(u_2 = g(b)\). Evaluating a \(u\)-integral using original \(x\)-limits is an automatic method loss on Cambridge Paper 3.

question.en: Use the substitution \(u = 2x + 1\) to find the exact value of \(\displaystyle\int_0^4 \frac{x}{\sqrt{2x+1}}\,dx\).

solution.en:
Let \(u = 2x + 1\), so \(du = 2\,dx \implies dx = \frac{1}{2}\,du\), and \(x = \frac{u - 1}{2}\).

Change limits:

\[x = 0 \implies u = 1,\quad x = 4 \implies u = 9\]

Transform the integral:

\[\int_0^4 \frac{x}{\sqrt{2x+1}}\,dx = \int_1^9 \frac{\frac{u - 1}{2}}{\sqrt{u}}\cdot\frac{1}{2}\,du = \frac{1}{4}\int_1^9 \left(u^{1/2} - u^{-1/2}\right)\,du\]\[= \frac{1}{4}\left[ \frac{2}{3}u^{3/2} - 2u^{1/2} \right]_1^9 = \frac{1}{4}\left( \left(\frac{2}{3}(27) - 2(3)\right) - \left(\frac{2}{3}(1) - 2(1)\right) \right)\]\[= \frac{1}{4}\left( (18 - 6) - \left(-\frac{4}{3}\right) \right) = \frac{1}{4}\left(12 + \frac{4}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{4}\left(\frac{40}{3}\right) = \frac{10}{3}\]
